newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 6.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 6.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Tuesday and main factors likely to affect trading:

* Manila shares are likely to edge higher on carry-over buying as investors unable to participate in Monday's dramatic rise will join the fray, said Lawrence de Leon, analyst at Dharmala Securities Phils.
* But pockets of profit-taking may be seen especially by investors who bought at the low-end. Local players are likely to dominate the market, said Bernard Gorospe, analyst at Citisecurities Inc.

* Sun Hung Kai Securities said in its daily outlook that for the technical recovery to be convincing, the stock market's main index must rally for three consecutive sessions backed by substantial volume.

* On Monday, the Philippine Stock Exchange composite index soared 130.77 points, or 5.02 percent, to 2,736.42 points snapping out of a six-day losing streak and posting the biggest single day rise in three years and five months.
* On Monday, the Dow Jones climbed 143.29 points to 7,214.49.
PLDT's ADR shed $0 7/8 to $55 1/4.
* The Central Bank raised the overnight borrowing rate to 11.50 percent from 11.0 percent but left its overnight lending rate unchanged at 12.65 percent.

* The National Statistics Office (NSO) announced on Monday a 4.6 percent inflation in April, down 4.8 percent in March surprising economists who expecting a slight acceleration following a series of oil price increases.
* Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said the government's inflation target for the year of six to seven percent was attainable.
* President Fidel Ramos assured investors who were pulling out of the country's stock market in droves last week that the economy remained on its upward path.

* International Monetary Fund Manila representative David Nellor said in a statement that the Philippines is not showing any signs of overheating and measures are in place to prevent any economic disruption.
* On Tuesday, the NSO said Philippine exports in March rose to $1.996 biillion from 41.67 billion a year ago.
* The Philippine 91-day treasury bill rate rose to 10.822 percent at the regular weekly auction on Monday up from 10.39 percent the previous week, the Bureau of Treasury said.
* Urbancorp Realty Developers Inc said it posted a net income of 28.367 million pesos in the first quarter of the year.
* Mondragon International Philippines Inc said it had settled its row with state-run Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corp over the operation of its casino inside a freeport area, north of Manila.
* Hi-Cement Corp said it generated a net income of 276.51 million pesos during its nine-month operation ending March 31.
* The Department of Finance said in a final report that the Philippines posted a 4.8 billion peso public sector surplus by the end of 1996.
* Globe Telecom said it earmarked $77.45 million this year to finance the installation of 170 new receiving stations to expand coverage of its mobile phone service.
* The Supreme Court on Monday dismissed a petition by the head of the National Telecommunications Commission and paved the way for a licence for local firm Bell Telecommunications Philippines.
* Newspaper Manila Times said MUSIC Semiconductors Corp's first quarter profits reached 19.4 million pesos, slightly higher than the 19 million pesos the company earlier projected.

* Newspaper BusinessWorld said the Securities and Exchange Commission issued a temporary restraining order preventing the management of the Medical City to enter into a strategic partnership with Benpres Holdings Corp.
* Today said newly-appointed PSE president Jose Luis Yulo said the exchange is ready for self-regulation although there is no hurry to reapply for self-regulatory organisation status.
* The peso closed lower at 26.365 to the dollar vs 26.374
* The Philippine interbank call loan average rose to 11.53125 percent from 11.0625 percent.
